<reason>B better distinguished enforceable oversight from the specific standardized-publication mandate. A established plausible transparency benefits, but repeatedly mischaracterized B’s alternative as either conceding the motion or withholding useful information from deployers. B answered that pressure directly and challenged both the claimed verification benefits and A’s minimal-cost framing. A’s closing preserved a public-accountability argument but did not adequately resolve those objections.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s response to A’s proposed public audit mechanism was decisive: finding failures through an API cannot disprove an aggregate refusal rate without knowing the underlying task distribution. This directly weakened A’s claim that redacted summaries enable outsiders to catch gaming, while preserving B’s distinction between useful disclosure and substantive independent scrutiny.</best_rebuttal>
